history.fix: The cart, the parts in it and the bin, rebuilt on the model building games use. The cart is a tray of tiles with tabs across the top (All, Devices, Tubing, Adapters, Interfaces); a tile is the part, its name, its connector shapes and how many are left, and the small print moved to the spec sheet a tap opens. The bin is gone from the wall: a Back to cart strip appears along the bottom only while you hold a part from the wall, and the cart lights up as a place to drop it. The buttons for a picked part carry their words under the icons: Turn, Flip, Details, Put back, Undo. The complexity stars are off the result card. The three cart changes are the new folder The cart at the top of the Device Assembly list.

history.note: This iteration is an improvement, and I do like the direction we are going. The challenge I have is that the phone view for it does not fit well within the windows or within the borders that we have pretty set. Is there a standard or a skill set or a training guide on how to design it's kind of like top down games or puzzle like games like this that are both web and phone friendly I think we're almost there on the design of the mechanics and the menuing at which point we can start to really dig into the games levels level design and the different kind of pathways we want to take

history.fix: On a phone held upright the game is now exactly the visible screen and nothing scrolls: the wall takes what is left and fits inside it, the bedside screen sits under it (your Round 16 pick), and Complete moved to the bottom right beside the cart's tabs, where a thumb is. My earlier phone tests used the whole 844 px of an emulated phone; Safari really leaves about 659 on an iPhone 15 with its bars up and 548 on an SE, so the cart fell off the bottom. Those real sizes are now checked on every puzzle-sheet run. Your question: there is no one standard, so I wrote the site's into the game skill (hu-game-shell, A phone is one screen) from web.dev on viewport units, the FIT mode web game engines use, and Apple's WWDC26 guidance on touch games. Level design and pathways are in the Inbox for when you want them. Check it in the new folder The screen.
